Department: Emergency Medicine

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Dark urine and fatigue three days after starting trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a skin infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 9-year-old male with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency returns one year after a prior hemolytic episode. Three days ago, he was treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a skin infection. His mother reports dark brown urine yesterday; he feels tired and looks pale today.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Folic acid 1 mg by mouth daily

ALLERGIES:

FAMILY HISTORY:
Family history is unremarkable.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, he is pale and mildly icteric with no hepatosplenomegaly.

LABORATORY DATA:
Labs show:
Hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL
Reticulocyte count 8%
Total bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL
Direct bilirubin 0.4 mg/dL
LDH Elevated
Haptoglobin Decreased

OTHER STUDIES:
A peripheral blood smear is shown below.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Leila Mahmoud, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Brought to the emergency department with jaundice and dark urine after eating fava beans at a family gathering two days ago.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
His 11-year-old sister, who also ate the same meal, developed similar symptoms including fatigue and pallor.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Folic acid 1 mg by mouth daily

ALLERGIES:
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, Fava beans

FAMILY HISTORY:
The boy's father is asymptomatic, and his mother reports that she occasionally experiences mild fatigue but has never had jaundice.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination of both children shows scleral icterus and splenomegaly.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies in both siblings reveal normocytic anemia with reticulocytosis and elevated lactate dehydrogenase levels. Peripheral smear demonstrates bite cells and Heinz bodies.

OTHER STUDIES:
Genetic testing confirms reduced activity of an X-linked red blood cell enzyme involved in protection against oxidative stress.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
The parents ask how their daughter could also be affected by what they were told is a "male disease."
